From: Liwei Song <liwei.song@windriver.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 12:00:35 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] firmware: stratix10-rsu: Fix NULL pointer dereference when
 RSU is disabled

When the Remote System Update (RSU) isn't enabled in the First Stage
Boot Loader (FSBL), the driver encounters a NULL pointer dereference when
excute svc_normal_to_secure_thread() thread, resulting in a kernel panic:

Unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at virtual address 0000000000000008

Hardware name: SoCFPGA Stratix 10 SoCDK (DT)

diff --git a/drivers/firmware/stratix10-rsu.c b/drivers/firmware/stratix10-rsu.c
index 41da07c445a6..e1912108a0fe 100644
--- a/drivers/firmware/stratix10-rsu.c
+++ b/drivers/firmware/stratix10-rsu.c
@@ -768,7 +768,9 @@ static int stratix10_rsu_probe(struct platform_device *pdev)
 				 rsu_async_status_callback);
 	if (ret) {
 		dev_err(dev, "Error, getting RSU status %i\n", ret);
+		stratix10_svc_remove_async_client(priv->chan);
 		stratix10_svc_free_channel(priv->chan);
+		return ret;
 	}
 
 	/* get DCMF version from firmware */
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### Modifications in `drivers/firmware/stratix10-rsu.c`

- **Added** `stratix10_svc_remove_async_client(priv->chan);` before `stratix10_svc_free_channel(priv->chan);` within the error handling block after a failed `stratix10_svc_request_channel_byname()` call.
- **Added** `return ret;` after `stratix10_svc_free_channel(priv->chan);` to immediately exit the probe function upon failure.

### Relationship Between the Modifications

The two modifications together form a complete error cleanup path. Previously, when retrieving the RSU status failed, the driver would free the service channel (`stratix10_svc_free_channel`) but did **not** remove the asynchronous client registration (`stratix10_svc_remove_async_client`). This left the thread `svc_normal_to_secure_thread` with a reference to an already freed channel, causing a NULL pointer dereference when that thread later tried to access the channel. By adding the missing cleanup call and returning an error code, the patch ensures that:
1. The asynchronous client is properly unregistered before the channel is freed.
2. The probe function does not continue after the failure, preventing the kernel from attempting to use an invalid channel later.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
<text>if (ret) {</text>

<text>    stratix10_svc_free_channel(priv->chan);</text>

Reason:
<text>This code frees the service channel without first removing the asynchronous client. Because the async client remains registered, the kernel thread svc_normal_to_secure_thread still holds a reference to the freed channel and later dereferences it, causing a NULL pointer dereference. Additionally, the function does not return early, allowing the probe to continue and register the thread.</text>

The code statements that fix the bug are:
<text>if (ret) {</text>
<text>    dev_err(dev, "Error, getting RSU status %i\n", ret);</text>
<text>    stratix10_svc_remove_async_client(priv->chan);</text>
<text>    stratix10_svc_free_channel(priv->chan);</text>
<text>    return ret;</text>
<text>}</text>
Reason:
<text>By calling stratix10_svc_remove_async_client before stratix10_svc_free_channel, the async client is properly deregistered, preventing the kernel thread from accessing the freed channel. The early return ensures that the probe function stops execution and does not register the thread or perform any further operations that depend on the now-invalid channel.</text>

The issue occurs because rsu_send_async_msg() fails when RSU is not enabled
in firmware, causing the channel to be freed via stratix10_svc_free_channel().
However, the probe function continues execution and registers
svc_normal_to_secure_thread(), which subsequently attempts to access the
already-freed channel, triggering the NULL pointer dereference.

Fix this by properly cleaning up the async client and returning early on
failure, preventing the thread from being used with an invalid channel.
